summary: Correctness hazards in source/cli/src (release/6.1.0 @ 007473ad). I checked each finding by running the container dist (/workspaces/Yggdrasil/source/cli/dist/bin.js) against scratch projects $TMPDIR/ch-sup, $TMPDIR/ch-mono, $TMPDIR/ch-case and $TMPDIR/ch-nocommit. Two findings also ran on the macOS host, from a copy of that same dist in the session scratchpad. What I found: seven confirmed defects with repros, plus one minor config-validation gap. The main themes: (a) hash and subject-set inputs that disagree with git or the host. The mapping walk misses .gitignore files that sit above the mapped directory. The log.md prefix hash is not line-ending normalized. The deterministic rule hash covers check.mjs but not the modules it imports. (b) Path identity: mapping entries are only lightly normalized (trim, backslash to slash, strip ./ and trailing slash), not canonicalized, so the filesystem-resolved subject set and the textual ownership model split on `a//b`, `a/./b`, `a/../a/b` and letter case. (c) Git path semantics: `git show <ref>:<path>` resolves from the repo root, while `ls-tree` and the callers work from cwd. This breaks `yg log merge-resolve` and `yg drill add` for any graph that sits below the git root. (d) Suppress-marker scope: a marker at the end of a code line waives the next line, not the line it sits on. Things I checked that held up: CLI errors on unreadable graph/lock files are loud, not swallowed. No EMFILE with 6,000 mapped files at ulimit 256. Porcelain/diff -z parsing is correct. Config sub-blocks reject unknown keys. Approve works with no commits and with no git. I did not repeat anything from the in-flight list.

surviving.title: Mapping expansion ignores .gitignore files between the repo root and the mapped directory, so gitignored build output is hashed, reviewed and turns CI red
surviving.where: source/cli/src/io/hash.ts:118-128 (local loadRootGitignoreStack: root .gitignore only), :212-225 (collectDirectoryFilePaths adds a .gitignore only for directories it walks from the mapping down), :293-297 (expandGlobEntry starts the walk at the glob base), :334-339 (directory branch); compare the coverage walk in io/repo-scanner.ts:55-99, which collects .gitignore files from the root down
surviving.evidence: In $TMPDIR/ch-sup: src/.gitignore holds `*.gen.ts`, and src/app/x.gen.ts is not in `git status`. With node mapping [src/app]: `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` reports `src/app/x.gen.ts:2: sync call`, while the header counts 3/7 files, so the coverage walk excludes the file. Changing only the mapping to [src]: the x.gen.ts violation disappears (the only remaining one is `src/a.ts:2`). Lock drift: with a clean x.gen.ts I approved and committed (`PASS ... 1 verified`). Then `rm src/app/x.gen.ts` (git status stays empty, because the file is ignored) and `yg check --no-approve` gives `FAIL ... unverified (not yet reviewed) ... app aspect 'no-sync'`, which is exactly what a fresh CI clone sees. Root cause: hash.ts carries its own copy of loadRootGitignoreStack/isIgnoredByStack. The comment at :136-137 says it 'Mirrors the C-27 fix in io/repo-scanner.ts', so this is hidden coupling. Separately, hash.ts:79 hashPath and :173 perFileHashes have no production callers (git grep finds them only in tests/unit/io/hash.test.ts), and they carry the same bug.
surviving.impact: The subject set and source fingerprint of any node mapped below a directory with its own .gitignore include untracked, ignored files (generated code, build output, local env files). An approved lock goes stale on every fresh clone and CI run, so the gate stays red and cannot be fixed from CI. The same files are also fed to deterministic checks and LLM reviewers, which then flag them. The same file is treated differently depending on whether the mapping is `src` or `src/app`.
surviving.suggested_fix: Delete the hash.ts copies. Have collectDirectoryFilePaths and expandGlobEntry seed their stack from the full root-to-baseDir chain of .gitignore files, using the one repo-scanner implementation. A shared `gitignoreStackFor(projectRoot, dir)` would do it. Add a regression test: nested .gitignore, a mapping below it, and a fingerprint that must match with the ignored file present and absent. Remove hashPath/perFileHashes, or route them through the same helper.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in the fresh project $TMPDIR/verify-correctness-hazards-1. With src/.gitignore holding `*.gen.ts` and node app mapped to [src/app], `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` refused with `src/app/x.gen.ts:2: sync call`, while the header counted `3/7 files`, so the coverage walk excludes the file. Next I made x.gen.ts clean, approved (PASS, 1 verified) and committed. After `rm src/app/x.gen.ts`, git status stayed empty and `yg check --no-approve` gave `FAIL ... unverified (not yet reviewed) ... app aspect 'no-sync'`. The code matches: hash.ts:118-128 loadRootGitignoreStack reads only the root .gitignore, and collectDirectoryFilePaths at :212-225 adds a .gitignore only for directories at or below the walk start. hashPath and perFileHashes are dead: git grep finds no callers outside hash.ts and tests/unit/io/hash.test.ts. It is not on the in-flight list. Downgraded from blocker because the trigger is narrow and has a workaround. It needs a .gitignore strictly between the repo root and the mapped directory; a .gitignore inside the mapped directory is honored. Adding the pattern to the root .gitignore, or mapping at the directory that holds the .gitignore, avoids it. The damage is still real: LLM-pair fingerprints go stale on a clean CI clone, and ignored files get reviewed.

surviving.title: log.md prefix_hash is taken over raw bytes, so a CRLF checkout (the Git for Windows default) fails log-integrity, and the suggested fix recreates the problem
surviving.where: source/cli/src/core/log/log-gate.ts:118-128 (computeLogBaselineFromContent: `Buffer.from(content,'utf-8').subarray(0, newest.offsetEnd)`); source/cli/src/core/log-integrity.ts:36-39 (validateAppendOnly, same raw bytes); io/graph-fs.ts:12-13 (readTextFile does not normalize). By contrast, io/hash.ts:26-38 normalizes CRLF for every source, rule and observation hash, 'so a verdict survives a line-ending change'.
surviving.evidence: In $TMPDIR/ch-sup: `yg log add --node app ...`, then `yg check --approve` (PASS), then commit. To simulate an autocrlf checkout: `sed -i 's/$/\r/' .yggdrasil/model/app/log.md`. `yg check --no-approve` then gives `FAIL ... log-integrity ... Log integrity broken (prefix_modified) at .yggdrasil/model/app/log.md`, with `Fix: Restore from git: git checkout HEAD -- .yggdrasil/model/app/log.md .yggdrasil/yg-lock.logs.json`. The .gitattributes that init writes (cat $TMPDIR/ch-sup/.gitattributes) pins eol only for lock/jsonl paths, and nothing for model/**/log.md.
surviving.impact: On Windows with core.autocrlf=true, which is the Git for Windows installer default, every node with a baselined log fails `yg check` with a history-tampering error right after a clean clone. The prescribed `git checkout HEAD --` writes CRLF again, so the adopter is stuck and is told their history was rewritten.
surviving.suggested_fix: Normalize line endings (normalizeLineEndings) before parseLog offsets and before the prefix hash, both when writing the baseline and when validating it. Keep compatibility with existing LF-written baselines: they hash the same after normalization. Also have init/upgrade add `/.yggdrasil/model/**/log.md text eol=lf` to .gitattributes.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced with a real autocrlf checkout, not with sed. In $TMPDIR/verify-correctness-hazards-1 I ran `yg log add --node app --reason ...` and `yg check --approve`, which wrote yg-lock.logs.json with a prefix_hash, then committed. Then `git config core.autocrlf true; rm log.md; git checkout -- log.md`. od shows `]  \r  \n` and git status is clean. `yg check --no-approve` then gives `FAIL ... log-integrity ... Log integrity broken (prefix_modified)` with `Fix: Restore from git: git checkout HEAD -- .yggdrasil/model/app/log.md .yggdrasil/yg-lock.logs.json`. Following that Fix exactly still fails with `prefix_modified`, so the adopter is stuck. The code matches: log-gate.ts:118-128 and log-integrity.ts:36-39 hash raw `Buffer.from(content,'utf-8')`, and graph-fs.ts readTextFile does not normalize. The .gitattributes that init writes has no eol rule for log.md. Git for Windows installs with autocrlf=true by default, so blocker holds. It is not in flight.

surviving.title: Deterministic verdict identity covers only check.mjs bytes, so an edit to a module that check.mjs imports leaves a stale cached verdict
surviving.where: source/cli/src/core/pair-inputs.ts:45-47 (ruleHashFor hashes only the check.mjs artifact); core/fill-det.ts:238; structure/hook-loader.ts:209-216 (plain dynamic import from the aspect dir); ast/loader-hook-impl.ts:8-21 (only `@chrisdudek/yg/*` is redirected, so relative and bare imports resolve normally)
surviving.evidence: In $TMPDIR/ch-sup: aspect max-lines has check.mjs `import { LIMIT } from "./limit.mjs"` and limit.mjs `export const LIMIT = 100;`. Approve gives `PASS ... 2 verified`. Then `echo 'export const LIMIT = 1;' > limit.mjs`: `yg check --no-approve` still says PASS, and `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` also says PASS (the check is not re-run). After adding one comment line to check.mjs: `[det] max-lines on node:app — refused ... src/app/ok.ts:1: too long`. Nothing in writing-deterministic-aspects knowledge or docs/reviewers.md forbids relative imports. By the same code path, the version of the CLI's own `@chrisdudek/yg/ast` and the grammar wasm files are not in computeDetInputHash (core/pair-hash.ts:212-231) either (read from code, not reproduced).
surviving.impact: Shared helper modules are the natural way to factor rules. With them, tightening a rule silently does nothing locally: the gitignored det cache keeps the old verdicts, while a fresh CI clone re-runs the rule and fails. The result is 'green on my machine, red in CI', or the reverse, with no signal about the cause.
surviving.suggested_fix: Either (a) fold the transitive local import closure of check.mjs/companion.mjs into the rule hash: hash every file under the aspect directory, or resolve the static imports, and include the CLI's version or grammar digest; or (b) reject any import other than `@chrisdudek/yg/*` and node builtins at load time with a clear error. Option (a) with a whole-aspect-dir hash is the simpler one to get right.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. Aspect max-lines has check.mjs `import { LIMIT } from "./limit.mjs"`, with LIMIT=100, approved and committed (2 verified). After changing limit.mjs to LIMIT=1, both `yg check --no-approve` and `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` still report `2 verified`, and the check does not re-run. Appending one comment line to check.mjs gives `[det] max-lines on node:app — refused` and `src/app/ok.ts:1: too long`. pair-inputs.ts:45-47 ruleHashFor hashes only contentFor(aspect,'check.mjs'). No docs forbid relative imports: a git grep of docs and source found no guidance either way. The det cache is gitignored, so a fresh CI clone re-runs the rule and can disagree with the local result. Major is appropriate.

surviving.title: A suppress marker at the end of a code line waives the NEXT line, not its own, in grammar-backed files; raw-scanned files do not treat it as a marker at all
surviving.where: source/cli/src/ast/suppress.ts:311-325 (AST path matches each comment node's own text, so a trailing `// yg-suppress(...)` starts with a delimiter and matches), :355-357 (single marker gives startLine = endLine = m.line + 1); the raw path at :336-341 needs the delimiter at the start of the physical line, so the same text after code is ignored there
surviving.evidence: src/a.ts line 2: `const a = fs.readFileSync("x"); // yg-suppress(no-sync) legacy trailing marker`; line 3: `const b = fs.readFileSync("y");`. `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` gives `enforced ... src/a.ts:2: sync call`. So line 2, the annotated one, still fails, and line 3 was silently waived. `yg suppressions` lists `line 2: single(no-sync) — legacy trailing marker` and never names the line it actually waives. docs/reviewers.md:580 says only that the marker 'must begin its comment line (after the comment delimiter)', which the trailing form satisfies literally.
surviving.impact: The most common suppression idiom in other linters (eslint-disable-line, # noqa, // NOLINT) waives the wrong line. The line the author meant stays red, which invites a second marker, and the following line gets an unreviewed, invisible waiver. Grammar and non-grammar files also disagree on the same text.
surviving.suggested_fix: In the AST path, check whether the comment node shares its row with a non-comment token. If it does, either apply the waiver to that same line or reject it with a diagnostic ('trailing yg-suppress is not supported; put it on the line above'). Have `yg suppressions` print the resolved waived range next to each marker.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. src/app/b.ts has line 2 `const a = fs.readFileSync("x"); // yg-suppress(no-sync) legacy trailing marker` and line 3 `const b = fs.readFileSync("y");`. Check output lists only `src/app/b.ts:2: sync call`, so line 3's violation is silently waived. `yg suppressions` shows `line 2: single(no-sync) — legacy trailing marker` and does not name the line it waives. docs/reviewers.md says a single marker waives the immediately following line, so the waived range follows the docs literally. The AST path (suppress.ts:311-325) nonetheless accepts a marker after code, while the raw path's own comment (:328-331) says a marker-shaped token after code is not a marker. The two paths disagree, and the common trailing-comment idiom from other linters produces an invisible waiver on an unrelated line. That is a real gate-integrity hazard. It is distinct from the in-flight reason-less marker issue.

surviving.title: Mapping entries are not canonicalized: `src//app` or a case-mismatched `SRC/App` (on macOS) makes the node review files that ownership and coverage say no node maps
surviving.where: source/cli/src/utils/mapping-path.ts:13-19 (normalizeMappingPath: trim, backslash to slash, strip ./ and trailing slash, but no collapse of `//`, `/./`, `x/../x`, and no check that the letter case matches the real path); io/hash.ts:330-339 (expansion goes through path.join and stat, which resolve these); ownership/coverage matches mapping text by prefix (mappingEntryMatchesFile)
surviving.evidence: (1) Linux container, mapping ["src//app"]: `yg check` says `1/7 files (0 node-owned, 3 type-covered)` with `1 verified`. `yg context --node app` lists `Source files (1): src/app/ok.ts`, while `yg owner --file src/app/ok.ts` says `No node maps this file`. (2) macOS host (APFS, case-insensitive), mapping ["SRC/App"] and a type whose when is `**/*.ts`: `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` gives `PASS ... (0 node-owned, 2 type-covered) ... 1 verified`. `yg owner --file SRC/App/ok.ts` gives `-> app`, and `yg owner --file src/app/ok.ts` gives `No node maps this file`. After committing and running the same tree on Linux: `FAIL ... mapping-path-missing` plus `type-when-mismatch`.
surviving.impact: Two models of 'which files this node owns' disagree. The pair and review side sees the files, while coverage, owner, type-level classification and relation ownership do not. A file can then be enforced both as node-owned and as type-covered, or be reported unowned. On case-insensitive filesystems a developer gets green locally and CI on Linux fails with a misleading message.
surviving.suggested_fix: Canonicalize mapping entries at parse time with path.posix.normalize (and reject any entry that still contains `..`). On load, compare each non-glob entry with the real on-disk spelling (a readdir walk, or realpath.native) and raise a blocking `mapping-path-case-mismatch` error, so the answer does not depend on the host filesystem.
surviving.verifier: The Linux part reproduced. With mapping ["src//app"] (and also "src/./app"), `yg check` reports `(0 node-owned, 3 type-covered ...)` while `yg context --node app` lists `Source files (1): src/app/ok.ts`, and `yg owner --file src/app/ok.ts` says `-> type:service ... No node maps this file`. normalizeMappingPath (mapping-path.ts:13-19) does not collapse `//` or `/./`. I did not reproduce the macOS case-mismatch part: the host dist is stale, and I did not run it. Downgraded because the trigger is a malformed mapping string an adopter rarely writes. The consequence is double-classification and a wrong owner answer, not a missed enforcement: the node's rules still run on the file. For the case variant, Linux CI fails loudly with mapping-path-missing, which is accurate there, so nothing slips through silently.

surviving.title: `yg log merge-resolve` and `yg drill add` fail for any graph below the git top level: `git show <ref>:<path>` resolves from the repo root, while the ls-tree fallback and the callers work from cwd
surviving.where: source/cli/src/utils/git-introspect.ts:59-89 (getFileAtRef: `git show ref:filePath`, then on failure `git ls-tree ref -- filePath` with cwd = projectRoot, which finds the path and rethrows), :114-155 (readFileAtCommit: same mismatch, returns not-at-commit); callers core/log/log-merge-resolve.ts:111-123 (`.yggdrasil/model/<node>/log.md`, graph-relative) and cli/log.ts:262-263 (repoRoot = path.dirname(graph.rootPath)), cli/drill-add.ts:101
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/ch-mono: git root with the graph in app/. Branches ours and theirs each ran `yg log add`, the merge conflicted in app/.yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md, I resolved it by union and committed. `cd app && yg log merge-resolve --node svc` gives `Could not read .yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md from the two sides of the merge ... Check the refs with git rev-parse` (exit 1). Direct check from app/: `git show HEAD:.yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md` gives `fatal: path 'app/.yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md' exists, but not '.yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md'`, while `git ls-tree HEAD -- .yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md` lists the blob. `yg drill add --aspect r --violates src/a.ts@HEAD` and `--violates app/src/a.ts@HEAD` both give `'…' is not in commit HEAD`.
surviving.impact: Monorepo and nested-graph adopters cannot reconcile log.md after a merge with the documented tool. They also cannot add drill cases with either path form. The error messages send them to check refs or paths that are actually fine. Progressive mode avoids this only because it explicitly declines subdirectory graphs.
surviving.suggested_fix: In getFileAtRef/readFileAtCommit, use the `<ref>:./<path>` form (resolved from cwd), or prefix the path with the value from getToplevelAndPrefix(). Use the same resolved path for both `git show` and `ls-tree`. Add tests that run from a subdirectory graph.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-correctness-hazards-mono, with the git root at the top and the graph in app/. The ours and theirs branches each ran `yg log add`; the merge conflicted in app/.yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md, which I resolved by union and committed. `cd app && yg log merge-resolve --node svc` gives `Could not read .yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md from the two sides of the merge ... Check the refs with git rev-parse`, exit=1. From app/, `git show HEAD:.yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md` gives `fatal: path 'app/.yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md' exists, but not '.yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md'`, and git itself hints `HEAD:./...`. `git ls-tree HEAD -- .yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md` lists the blob. The code matches: git-introspect.ts getFileAtRef uses `${ref}:${filePath}`, the ls-tree fallback finds the path, and it rethrows. readFileAtCommit, which drill add uses, has the same ls-tree/show mismatch and returns not-at-commit (read from the code; I did not run drill add). The error message sends the adopter to check refs that are fine. It is not in flight.

surviving.title: Unknown top-level keys in yg-config.yaml are silently ignored, while every sub-block rejects unknown keys
surviving.where: source/cli/src/io/config-parser.ts:194-247 (parseConfig reads raw.version, raw.quality, raw.reviewer, … and never checks the top-level key set); compare :56-64 (coverage), :140, :321, :360, :420, :511, :667, which all reject unknown keys with the stated reason 'a silently ignored typo means … enforcement quietly differs from what the config appears to say'
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/ch-sup: appending `progresive:\n  reference: main\nparalel: 8` gives no mention in `yg check` output, and `yg check --json` shows `progressive: null`. Replacing `auto_approve: false` with `autoapprove: true` is also silent. `coverage: { requried: [src] }` is correctly refused with `config-coverage-unknown-key`.

summary:
Concurrency/IO audit of the Yggdrasil CLI on release/6.1.0 at 007473ad. I read atomic-write, lock-store, fill-writer, fill-pool, fill-llm-phase, cli-base and the CLI providers, events-store/reader, log-store/log-add/aspect-log/aspect-status, det-worker-pool, docs/concurrency.md and docs/the-lock.md. Everything was tried against the live dist in the dev container, in scratch projects $TMPDIR/ci-p1..p3 with a fake `claude`/`gemini` on PATH (no API keys), plus a throwaway clone of the dogfood repo for timing.

**What holds up:**
- Temp names are unique, so atomic rename works.
- A SIGKILL in the middle of a fill keeps a valid lock: 2,639 det verdicts survived and the file parsed.
- The per-pair persistence survives interruption, as documented.

**What breaks is the error paths around child processes, streams and the write chain:**
- Neither the reviewer's stdin nor the process's own stdout/stderr has an error handler, so an EPIPE crashes the whole run.
- The reviewer timeout does not actually bound a call.
- One failed lock write poisons every later write in the run.
- Lock persistence is quadratic.
- `--only-deterministic` does write a committed file.
- A `check.mjs` that never finishes hangs the keyless gate forever.
- Concurrent `yg log add` silently loses entries.

Items already in flight were left out.

surviving.title: Reviewer that exits without reading stdin crashes the whole --approve run (unhandled EPIPE on child.stdin)
surviving.where: source/cli/src/llm/cli-base.ts:274-276 (child.stdin.write(prompt) with no 'error' listener on child.stdin)
surviving.evidence: Fake `claude` answers `--version` with exit 0 but exits 1 on the real call without reading stdin, which is how a CLI that rejects an unknown flag or an expired login behaves. `yg check --approve` on 40 LLM pairs with parallel: 8 printed '... 10/40 filled (0 ok, 10 infra)' and then died: `node:events:497 throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event ... Error: write EPIPE ... at ClaudeCodeProvider.verifyAspect (dist/bin.js:21108)`. Exit 1, no report, no Next: line, and the GC/closure steps never ran. Mode 'exit 0 without reading' crashed the same way. Whether a given run crashes or just records infra depends on timing.
surviving.impact: When the reviewer breaks fast, the adopter gets a raw Node stack about a pipe instead of the infra message that names the provider. Every run can crash at a random point, so the failure is hard to diagnose, and in-flight sibling reviewer calls are orphaned.
surviving.suggested_fix: Attach `child.stdin.on('error', …)` that records the error (EPIPE counts as infra) and lets 'close'/'exit' settle the promise. Consider writing the prompt with a callback so a write error is folded into the fallback response.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced three times out of three in $TMPDIR/verify-concurrency-io-c1 (40 nodes, parallel 8). The fake `claude` answers --version with exit 0 and otherwise does `exit 1` without reading stdin. Each run printed '... 40/80 filled (40 ok)' and then `node:events:497 throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event ... Error: write EPIPE ... at ClaudeCodeProvider.verifyAspect (dist/bin.js:21108)`, exit 1, with no report and no nondet lock written. In the source, cli-base.ts:274-276 calls `child.stdin.write(prompt); child.stdin.end();` and nothing listens for 'error' on child.stdin. This is not in the in-flight list, which only covers stderr/HTTP status being lost from messages. It crashed every time, not just now and then.

surviving.title: Reviewer timeout does not bound a call: 'close' waits on any grandchild holding the pipes, and only the direct child is killed
surviving.where: source/cli/src/llm/cli-base.ts:221-272 (spawn without detached/process-group kill; resolution only in child.on('close'); stdout decoded per chunk with data.toString())
surviving.evidence: Tier config `timeout: 3` (seconds, config-parser.ts:694 multiplies by 1000). (a) Fake claude that forks `sleep 1000 &` and then blocks: `timeout 60 yg check --approve` was killed at 60s (`EXIT=124 after 60s`), last output '... still working (0/1, waiting on llm-a on node:m01)'. SIGTERM/SIGKILL hit only the direct child, and 'close' never fires while the grandchild holds stdout. (b) Fake claude that prints a valid verdict, exits 0 at once and leaves `(sleep 30) &` behind: the run took 30s (`EXIT=1 after 30s`), and the verdict was thrown away as 'Reviewer for aspect llm-a on node:m01 returned a provider error: Reviewer unavailable', because the 3s timer had set killed=true while 'close' was still pending.
surviving.impact: A reviewer CLI that leaves helper processes behind (tool subprocesses, MCP/servers, update checkers) either hangs `yg check --approve` with no upper bound, or turns a paid, valid verdict into infra after waiting out the helper's lifetime. The configured timeout promises a bound it does not deliver.
surviving.suggested_fix: Spawn with `detached: true` and kill the process group (`process.kill(-pid, sig)`) on timeout. Settle on 'exit' plus a short bounded drain of stdout instead of waiting on 'close' without limit. Only discard the output when the timeout fired before the child exited. Also use `child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8')` so multi-byte characters split across chunks are not corrupted.
surviving.verifier: The mechanism is real. In $TMPDIR/verify-concurrency-io-c2 with timeout: 3: (a) a fake that runs `sleep 1000 &` and then blocks was still running when `timeout 30` killed it (EXIT=124 after 30s). (b) A fake that prints a valid verdict, exits 0 and leaves `(sleep 20) &` behind took 20s, and its verdict was thrown away as 'returned a provider error: Reviewer unavailable'. The code shows why: the promise only resolves on 'close', and `child.kill` reaches the direct child only (cli-base.ts:221-272), even though the comment there says 'so the reviewer call always terminates'. But nobody showed that a real provider leaves helper processes holding the stdout pipe. claude-code runs with `--tools ''`, an empty MCP config and no session persistence, so the trigger is hypothetical. That makes it minor. The utf8-split-across-chunks point is also real (data.toString() per chunk) and also minor.

surviving.title: One failed lock write poisons the serialized write chain for the rest of the run; later paid verdicts are discarded and reported as unaffected infra

summary:
Architecture and design of source/cli/src (release/6.1.0, 007473ad). How the code is laid out: 13 top-level dirs, about 82k prod lines. core/ is 97 files and 25.6k lines, cli/ 43 files and 16.8k lines, templates/ 8.5k, io/ 8.1k, relations/ 7.4k, portal/ 5.0k. The layers are mostly clean. No core/io/utils/model module imports cli/. core/ has no process.exit, and io→core is limited to one type-only import. The one upward edge is portal/engine-api.ts → cli/preamble, cli/rules-artifacts and cli/group-issues, and it causes a real crash (F1).

Wider problems:
- Logic that belongs in core sits in CLI action bodies. The command actions are the largest functions in the codebase: check 453 lines, impact 453, aspect-test 365, context 258, init 256. Only half of all logic lives in core.
- The graph's relation rules push code into literal copies and pass-through wrappers instead of declared edges.
- Lock persistence has no concurrency control and rewrites the whole lock once per verdict.

All findings were checked in the dev container, in scratch projects under $TMPDIR/archdesign-* and in a clone of the repo at $TMPDIR/archdesign-ygg. The repo's own graph passes: `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` gives PASS, 473 nodes, 5663 verified. Several of these defects sit behind that green check, and in F2 a test locks the wrong behaviour in.

surviving.title: The schema-version gate can be bypassed: an unquoted numeric or absent `version:` loads as the current schema, and three readers disagree
surviving.where: source/cli/src/core/migrator.ts:23-36 (detectVersion: `typeof raw.version === 'string'` else null); source/cli/src/core/graph-loader.ts:137-150 (every gate is conditioned on `detected !== null`); source/cli/src/io/config-parser.ts:228 (same string-only read; config.version has 0 consumers); source/cli/src/cli/simulate.ts:207 (regex reader)
surviving.evidence:
The loader's comment says a malformed version 'fails CLOSED'. But YAML parses `version: 5.1` as a number, so detectVersion returns null and the gate is skipped.

Container runs of `yg check --no-approve` with only the version line changed:
- `version: "5.1"` → exit=1 'not valid semver'
- `version: 5.1` → exit=0
- `version: 5` → exit=0
- `version: "99.0.0"` → exit=1 'newer than this CLI supports'
- `version: 99.0` → exit=0
- version line deleted → exit=0

surviving.evidence: The utility type says "Pure helper utilities — no I/O", yet utils/git.ts imports execFileSync, and git-introspect.ts, git-pack-fetch.ts (clones a remote into destDir) and binary-check.ts import execFile from node:child_process.
